summary_html: A **judge orders** CPS to investigate or assess during civil/criminal proceedings. Federal funding statutes (ASFA/IV-E) tether court findings to child-welfare actions, embedding judicial oversight into intake-to-case flow.
authority_html:
- **ASFA (42 U.S.C. §§ 671–675)** — court ‘reasonable efforts’ findings; permanency timelines  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funding structure linking court oversight to agency actions

key_cases.case_name: Amy S. v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: Assuming without deciding that the superior court violated due process by taking judicial notice of contested facts, pleadings, and testimony from the parents' domestic-relations file when adjudicating the child in need of aid, any error was harmless, and the adjudication was affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: Addresses AS 47.10.113, which folds custody questions into the CINA case, and limits how the custody file may be used.
key_cases.quote: taking judicial notice of the existence of ten years of custody disputes is different than taking judicial notice of specific facts, pleadings, and testimony from the custody case

mandatory_reporters: Practitioners of the healing arts — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a)(1)

School teachers and school administrative staff of public and private schools, including athletic coaches — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a)(2); an unpaid volunteer athletic coach is not required to report unless the coach volunteers more than four hours a week for four consecutive weeks or more than 20 hours a week in a one-month period, has received the training required under Alaska Stat. § 47.17.022, and has signed a form acknowledging the duty to report — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(j)
Peace officers and officers of the Department of Corrections — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a)(3)
Administrative officers of institutions — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a)(4)
Paid employees of domestic violence and sexual assault programs and of crisis intervention and prevention programs — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a)(6)
Paid employees of an organization that provides counseling or treatment to people seeking to control their use of drugs or alcohol — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a)(7)
Members of a child fatality review team or of the multidisciplinary child protection team — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a)(8)
Volunteers who interact with children in a public or private school for more than four hours a week — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a)(9)
Juvenile probation officers and juvenile probation office staff, and staff of juvenile detention and juvenile treatment facilities — Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a)(10)
reporting_details: Alaska is not a universal-reporting state: only the occupational categories listed in Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(a) are required to report, and they must report immediately — defined as no later than 24 hours (Alaska Stat. § 47.17.290(7)) — to the nearest office of the Department of Family and Community Services, the department in which the Office of Children's Services sits (Alaska Stat. § 47.17.290(6)); if the harm appears to result from a suspected sex offense they must also report immediately to the nearest law enforcement agency. A reporter who cannot reasonably contact the nearest office of the department when immediate action is necessary for the child's well-being must instead report to a peace officer (Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(c)). Any other person may report but is not required to (Alaska Stat. § 47.17.020(b)). OCS takes reports at 1-800-478-4444 or 907-269-6510, 24 hours a day, every day, and takes a written report by email at ReportChildAbuse@alaska.gov or by fax at 907-269-3939.
